lesson.child_mission: Day and night happen because Earth spins (rotates). The side facing the Sun has day; the side facing away has night.
lesson.evidence_instructions: Save the independent response, specific revisions and both short-answer explanations; record oral evidence for speaking tasks.

lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
If it is day where you are, what is likely on the opposite side of Earth?

FEEDBACK
Night (approximately opposite).

WATCH FOR
Thinking the Sun moves around Earth each day is a common alternative idea; the Year 3 model uses Earth’s spin.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Build a ball-and-torch day/night model. Draw day and night on a circle diagram. Write two sentences using spin/rotate language.

Write a short reflection naming one observation or step you corrected and why.

Parent: Written model 1: Original demonstration: Torch as Sun, ball as Earth: spin the ball — half lit, half dark. People on the lit side see day; on the dark side see night.

Parent: Written model 2: Common error: Thinking the Sun moves around Earth each day is a common alternative idea; the Year 3 model uses Earth’s spin. Correction: Night (approximately opposite).

Parent: Likely misconception: Thinking the Sun moves around Earth each day is a common alternative idea; the Year 3 model uses Earth’s spin. Keep sample answers out of the child role.
